gml:Dictionary.gml:description: This dictionary contains the values for the propertyClass property of the diggs:Property object and the measurand property of the diggs:Detector object when used within the Test and Monitor DIGGS features. These values serve to define the ultimate results of geotechnical and environmental tests and monitoring activities that result from test procedures and monitoring sensors. The Xpaths to these occurrences are: 1) //diggs:Property/diggs:propertyClass (for Test, MaterialTest or Monitor) 2)//diggs:Detector/diggs:measurand (for measurand).
gml:Dictionary.gml:name: DIGGS Measurement Properties

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The gauge gas pressure against the inside of the membrane when the center of the membrane has lifted above its support and moved laterally 0.05-mm (tolerance +0.02, -0.00 mm) into the soil surrounding the blade.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: A-Pressure

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The value of the AASHTO group index (GI) as defined by: GI= (F–35)[0.2+0.005(LL– 40)}+(F–15)(PI–10) where F is the percentage passing the 75 μm (0.075 mm) sieve, expressed as a whole number, LL is the liquid limit and PI is the plasticity index.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: AASHTO Group Index

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The group or appropriate subgroup classification as defined by AASHTO M145-91
diggs:Definition.gml:name: AASHTO Symbol

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A measure of the resistance of aggregate to surface wear by abrasion.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Aggregate Abrasion Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A relative measure of the resistance of an aggregate to crushing under a gradually applied compressive load.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Aggregate Crushing Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The ratio, (by mass) of particles whose greatest dimension (length) is 1.8 times their mean dimension to the total mass of the sample.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Aggregate Elongation Index

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Percentage (by mass) of aggregate particles whose least dimension is less than 0.6 times their mean size, to the total sample mass.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Aggregate Flakiness Index

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The resistance to impact of aggregates and is measured as the fraction of aggregates passing to the total mass of the sample.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Aggregate Impact Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The actual measured loss (difference between the original mass and the final mass of the test sample), expressed as a percentage of the original mass of the test sample.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Aggregate Los Angeles Abrasion Loss

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The loss (difference between the original weight and the final weight of the test sample), expressed as an integer.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Aggregate Los Angeles Coefficient

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The actual measured loss (difference between the original mass and the final mass of the test sample), expressed as an integer ratio of the original mass of the test sample.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Aggregate Los Angeles Wear Ratio

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A measure of the resistance of an aggregate to polishing.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Aggregate Polished Stone Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The amount of mass ost by degradation as determined by sieving and weighing the samples after the test cycles.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Aggregate Soundness Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A water content value that gives an idea of strength of aggregate. Aggregates having more water absorption are more porous in nature and are generally considered unsuitable unless they are found to be acceptable based on strength, impact, and hardness tests.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Aggregate Water Absorption

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The gauge gas pressure against the inside of the membrane when the center of the membrane has lifted above its support and moved laterally 1.10-mm (60.03 mm) into the soil surrounding the blade.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: B-Pressure

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The volume of clear water in a grout cylinder resulting from grout sedimentation, reported as a percentage of initial total column height.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Bleed

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The number of blows of a hammer that drives a tool into the earth for a particular distance. The distance should correspond to the difference between the associated top and bottom positions recorded in the location property of the test, or be specified in the pen_increment property associated with a point location.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Blow Count

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Total weight (of solids and water) divided by total volume of material, representing natural conditions. This is technically a unit weight not a density, but it is using the industry standard terminology assuming earth gravity. Value can also be reported in true density units (mass/volume)
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Density, Bulk (Natural)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The gauge gas pressure against the inside of the membrane when the center of the membrane returns to the A-pressure position during a controlled, gradual deflation following the B-pressure.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: C-Pressure

diggs:Definition.gml:description: California Bearing Ratio is the ratio, expressed as a percentage, of the measured pressure for site soils at a penetration of 0.100 in divided by pressure to achieve equal penetration on a standard soil.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Corrected Cbr At 0.100 in Penetration

diggs:Definition.gml:description: California Bearing Ratio is the ratio, expressed as a percentage, of the measured pressure for site soils at a penetration of 0.200 in divided by pressure to achieve equal penetration on a standard soil.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Corrected Cbr At 0.200 In Penetration

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The Chalk Crushing Value is determined by using the chalk impact crushing test, which measures the rate at which a sample of chalk lumps crushes under impacts from a freefalling rammer. The chalk crushing value can be used, together with the saturation moisture content of the intact chalk lumps, to classify chalk in relation to its behavior as a freshly placed fill material. The test procedure is described for a single sample of chalk lumps, but normal procedure should be to calculate the mean value derived from six such tests on representative samples.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Chalk Crushing Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Chloride content of soil or groundwater by laboratory testing (corrosivity series). USE THIS ENTRY WHEN THE SOURCE DOES NOT STATE THE EXTRACTION BASIS - the case for the Jazera project record (GBL-24136), which reports a chloride content as a percentage without saying whether it is water- or acid-soluble. Where the basis IS known, prefer chloride_water_soluble or chloride_acid_soluble instead.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Chloride Content

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Represents the total amount of clay sized particles (<2 microns) in a test samples, expressed as a percentage by mass, to the total sample
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Clay Fraction < 2 Micron

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Represents the total amount of clay sized particles (<5 microns) in a test samples, expressed as a percentage by mass, to the total sample
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Clay Fraction < 5 Micron

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The horizontal coefficient of consolidation as derived from the dissipation test data from a cone penetration or dilatometer test.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Coefficient of Horizontal Consolidation (Ch)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The vertical coefficient of consolidation as derived from a one-dimensional consolidation test in the lab.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Coefficient of Vertical Consolidation(Cv)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A coefficient describing the degree of curvature of the grain size distribution. Defined as (d30)^2/((d60)*(d10))
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Coefficient of Curvature

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The ratio of horizontal earth pressure to vertical pressure for a sample in the field.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Coefficient of Earth Pressure, In Situ

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The rate at which water flows through a soil is proportional to the hydraulic gradient and is expressed by Darcy's Law. Also known as the hydraulic conductivity. For lab tests, an average of measured values over several permeation trials.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Coefficient of Permeability

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Coefficient of permeability, corrected to 20 degrees C.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Coefficient of Permeability, Corrected

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Coefficient of permeability, measuring rate of horizontal flow
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Horizontal Coefficient of Permeability

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Coefficient of permeability, measuring rate of vertical flow
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Vertical Coefficient of Permeability

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The ratio of D60/D10
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Coefficient of Uniformity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Shear resistance at zero normal stress ?the portion of the shear strength of a soil indicated by the term c, in Coulomb's equation
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Peak Cohesion

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Shear resistance at zero normal stress at the residual (or large deformation) strength.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Residual Cohesion

diggs:Definition.gml:description: represents the total amount of <1 micron size particles in a test sample, as a percentage of the total sample mass
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Colloid Fraction

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Result from a Consolidation Test. This test is performed to determine the magnitude and rate of void ratio change for a laterally confined soil specimen that is subjected to different vertical pressures. From the measured data, the consolidation curve (pressure-void ratio relationship) can be plotted. This specific value is used for a specific portion of the log vertical pressure - void ratio curve to signify virgin compression. The one-dimension consolidation curve can be used to determine other values (e.g., the recompression index (slope of recompression curve) and the preconsolidation pressure (or maximum past pressure) of the soil).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Compression Index

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Result of axial compression test using unconfined compression
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Unconfined Compressive Strength

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A measure of the conductive power of a specified material to the flow of an electric current.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Conductivity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The consistency index (CI) indicates the consistency (firmness) of a soil. It is calculated as CI = (LL-W)/(LL-PL), where W is the natural water content. Soil at the liquid limit will have a consistency index of 0, while soil at the plastic limit will have a consistency index of 1.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Consistency Index

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Measure of slope of stress-strain curve when specimen is confined. Usually the result from a 1-D consolidation test.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Constrained Modulus, Vertical, Drained

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The particle diameter at which 10% of the particles in a soil or granular material sample are finer by weight.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: d10

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The particle diameter at which 15% of the particles in a soil or granular material sample are finer by weight.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: d15

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The particle diameter at which 30% of the particles in a soil or granular material sample are finer by weight.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: d30

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The particle diameter at which 50% of the particles in a soil or granular material sample are finer by weight.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: d50

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The particle diameter at which 60% of the particles in a soil or granular material sample are finer by weight.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: d60

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The particle diameter at which 85% of the particles in a soil or granular material sample are finer by weight.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: d85

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Volume of water divided by the volume of voids, expressed as a unitless ratio.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Degree of Saturation

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Duration of delay before the start of a penetration increment
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Delay Time

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Measured depth of the drill bit from the borehole centerline origin at time of measurement
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Depth

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The diffrence between the observed friction angle of a soil during dilation and the friction angle at zero dilation
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Dilation Angle

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Dilatometer modulus (Ed), based on linear elastic theory, and the primary index used in the correlation for the constrained and Young's moduli.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Dilatometer Modulus (Ed)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: DMT tip bearing (qD) is the axial thrust force at the end of a dilatometer blade divided by the projected cross-sectional area of the blade normal to the penetration. The DMT tip bearing is similar to the cone resistance, qc and may be used to evaluate stratigraphy. In cohesionless soils, qD and eD may be used to estimate the friction angle, overconsolidation ratio and at rest coefficient of earth pressure.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Dilatometer Tip Bearing

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Weight or mass of solids divided by total volume. This is technically a unit weight not a density, the value can also be reported in true density units.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Density, Dry

diggs:Definition.gml:description: This is a result of a compaction test. It is defined as the maximum dry density that is measured when a specific type and amount of energy is used for the compaction test. This is also the value of the compacted dry density when the soil is at the optimum moisture content. This is technically a unit weight not a density, but ithe value can also be reported in true density units.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Maximum Dry Density

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Vertical effective stress at the center of the membrane before the insertion of the DMT blade.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Vertical Effective Stress

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Amount of time since start of a measurement
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Elapsed Time

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Volume of filtrate extruded in Pressure Filtration test
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Filtrate Volume

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Flame Ionization Detector Test detects total concentrations of organic gases and vapors. Gases and vapors are ionized in a flame; a current is produced in proportion to the number of carbon atoms present. Reported result can be in various units of measure, depending upon specific equipment used.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Flame Ionization Measurement

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Time for grout specimen to exit flow cone
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Flow Cone Time

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The rate of fluid flow, measuredd as mass/time
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Mass Flow Rate

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The rate of fluid flow, measuredd as volume/time
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Volume Flow Rate

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Angle of friction at constant volume
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Critical State Friction Angle

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Measure of frictional resistance of soil. Ratio of shear strength to normal stress.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Peak Angle of Internal Friction

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Angle between the axis of normal stress and the tangent to the Mohr envelope at a point representing the failure-stress condition following large deformation
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Residual Angle of Internal Friction

diggs:Definition.gml:description: ratio of sleeve resistance to tip resistance
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Friction Ratio

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Test establishes the degree of frost-susceptibility of unbound sub-base and base materials for pavements.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Frost Heave

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Pressure measured with a gauge
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Gauge Pressure

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The time it takes for a chemical grout to gel. If determined by rotational viscometer, this is the value where viscosity reaches 100 mpa*s.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Gel Time

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Heavy fuel fluorescence detector value measured by sensor
diggs:Definition.gml:name: HFFD

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The dimensionless dilatometer horizontal stress index, the primary index used in the correlation for in-situ horizontal stress, overconsolidation ratio, and undrained shear strength in cohesive soils. KD is similar to the at-rest coefficient of earth pressure except that it includes blade penetration effects.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Horizontal Stress Index (Kd)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Measured inclination angle (vertical = 0 degrees); bearing unspecified or specified as another property
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Inclination

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Inclination measured in defined x direction (specified elsewhere)
diggs:Definition.gml:name: X Inclination

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Inclination measured in defined y direction (specified elsewhere)
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Y Inclination

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The horizontal component of the original stress status before excavations or other perturbations.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Insitu Horizontal Stress

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The Point Load Test produces an uncorrected Point Load Test Index (Is), which can be correlated with the uniaxial compressive strength (UCS) of rock.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Uncorrected Point Load Test Index

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The Point Load Test produces the Point Load Test Index (Is50), which can be correlated with the uniaxial compressive strength (UCS) of rock.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Size Corrected Point Load Test Index

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Light fuel fluorescence detector value measured by sensor
diggs:Definition.gml:name: LFFD

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The pressure at failure during a Pressuremeter test
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Limit Pressure

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Coefficient A computed for line loss regression equation Ax^2 + Bx + C
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Line Loss Coefficient A

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Coefficient B computed for line loss regression equation Ax^2 + Bx + C
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Line Loss Coefficient B

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Coefficient C computed for line loss regression equation Ax^2 + Bx + C
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Line Loss Coefficient C

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The correlation coefficient of the line loss regression equation
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Line Loss R2

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The liquid limit (LL) is the water content at which a soil changes from plastic to liquid behavior.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Liquid Limit

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Liquid limit determined if sample required oven drying before test
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Oven Dried Liquid Limit

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The liquidity index (LI) is used for scaling the natural water content of a soil sample to the limits. It can be calculated as a ratio of difference between natural water content, plastic limit, and liquid limit: LI=(W-PL)/(LL-PL) where W is the natural water content.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Liquidity Index

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The amount of organic matter in a soil that derives from peat, organic muck, plant material such as wood, roots, grass, or carbonaceous materials such as lignite, coal, etc.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Organic Content of Soil

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A unit devised to quantify the water permeability of bedrock and the hydraulic conductivity resulting from fractures. It is defined as the amount of water (in liters) that can be absorbed by a 1-meter length of a borehole per minute, at an over-pressure of 1 MPa (10 bar).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Lugeon Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Time for grout speciment to exit marsh funnel
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Marsh Funnel Time

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The mass of material observed
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Mass

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The amount of mass reduced between observation steps
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Mass Loss

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Unitless dilatometer material index, used to identify soil type and delineate stratigraphy.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Material Index s

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The Moisture Condition Value (MCV) is determined from a moisture condition test, a physical test indicating how much compactive effort is needed to compact a sample of soil at a particular moisture content.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Moisture Condition Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A measure of mass loss in dry aggregate
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Mean Micro Deval Value, dry

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A measure of mass loss in wet aggregate
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Mean Micro Deval Value, wet

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The pressuremeter modulus (E_M), a measure of soil deformability derived from the pseudo-elastic phase of the initial expansion curve of a Menard-type (prebored) pressuremeter test, per the test standard's prescribed interpretation. Distinct from the trial-level shearModulus (Gur), the unload/reload modulus derived from self-boring/cyclic pressuremeter interpretation over a different portion of the loading history; the two are related by a soil-dependent rheological factor, not an identity.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Menard Modulus (E_M)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Shear modulus, denoted by G, is defined as the ratio of shear stress to the shear strain.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Shear Modulus

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The tangent modulus of the initial, linear portion of a stress-strain curve for material in axial compression or tension is called Young's modulus, also known as the tensile (compression) modulus. It is defined as the ratio of the uniaxial stress over the uniaxial strain in the range of stress in which Hooke' Law holds. It is often calculated using theory of elasticity from other tests.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Young's Modulus

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Grout or mud density determined using a mud balance. While called a density, measurement is a force (weight) / voume but can also report this value in true density units (mass/volume)
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Mud Balance Density

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Value from Standard Penetration Test (SPT) to define advancement in terms of blows required to drive a specific sampler I foot into the soil using a hammer that provides a specific impact energy.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: N-Value (Raw)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Calculated value that corrects the value of the Standard Penetration Blow Count (N), to account for energy of the hammer (specifically normalized to 60% energy) and specific overburden conditions (specifically to an overburden stress of 1 ton per square foot).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: N1,60

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Calculated value that corrects the value of the Standard Penetration Blow Count (N-value), to account for energy of the hammer (specifically normalized to 60% energy).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: N60

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A value of true for this property indiates that no plastic limit can be . In such cases the value of the plastic limit should be left empty or set to the null value, and the value of non_plastic set to true.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Non Plastic

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A calculation that reflects the maximum past consolidation that the in situ soil has been subjected to compared to the current vertical overburden stress on the sample in the field. This value is usually measured from the one-dimensional consolidation tests. Often referenced as the parameter to track the stress history.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Overconsolidation Ratio

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The velocity of a p-wave (Vp). P-waves (primary waves) are compressional waves that are longitudinal in nature.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Primary Compression Wave Velocity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A-Reading corrected for the DA membrane stiffness at 0.05 mm expansion, the 0.05 mm expansion itself and the gauge pressure deviation from zero. This corrected pressure is referred to as p0. This is an intermediate result from a flat plate dilatometer test.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: P0 Reading

diggs:Definition.gml:description: B-Reading corrected for the DB membrane stiffness at 1.10 mm expansion and the gauge pressure deviation from zero. This corrected pressure is referred to as p1. This is an intermediate result from a flat plate dilatometer test.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: P1 Reading

diggs:Definition.gml:description: C-Reading corrected for the DA membrane stiffness at 0.05 mm expansion and the gauge pressure deviation from zero. This corrected pressure is referred to as p2. This is an intermediate result from a flat plate dilatometer test.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: P2 Reading

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The distance that a tool travels for a given number of hammer blows.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Penetration Increment

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The percentage by mass of particles larger than 3 inches (75 mm) and smaller than 12 inches (300 mm)
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Percent Cobbles

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The percentage of particles that pass through the #200 sieve (<0.075-mm).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Percent Fines

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The percentage of particles that are retained on the #4 and larger sizes (>4.75 mm).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Percent Gravel

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The percentage of particles thatpass the #4 sieve and are retained on the #200 sieve (<4.75 mm and >0.075-mm).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Percent Sand

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The percentage of particles smaller than 0.075 mm (No. 200 sieve) and larger than 0.002 mm and have a plotting position below the A-line on the plasticity chart as well as a plasticity index less than 4. The percent silt is determined by the difference between the total percent passing the No. 200 sieve (fines) and the percent clay (determined through plasticity testing of the fines fraction).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Percent Silt

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The negative base-10 logarithm of hydrogen ion activity in a soil-water suspension or in a water sample - the measure of how acidic or alkaline the material is, on a scale where 7 is neutral, lower values are acidic and higher values alkaline. Dimensionless by definition, so a Property carrying it states no uom. Determined electrometrically with a pH meter: BS 1377-3 Clause 12; ASTM G51 and AASHTO T 289 where the purpose is corrosion assessment; ASTM D4972 for agricultural, environmental and natural-resource purposes, whose own scope excludes corrosion testing. In a ground-aggressivity assessment pH is read together with resistivity, sulfate and chloride rather than on its own.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: pH

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Measures volatile organic compounds and other gases, expressed in parts per million or percent LEL
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Photoionization Detector Result
diggs:Definition.diggs:quantityClass: amount of substance per amount of substance

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The plastic limit (PL) is the water content where soil transitions between brittle and plastic behavior. A unitless value.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Plastic Limit

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The plasticity index (PI) is a measure of the plasticity of a soil. The plasticity index is a measure of the range of water contents where the soil exhibits plastic properties. The PI is the difference between the liquid limit and the plastic limit (PI = LL-PL). (Soils with a high PI tend to be clay, those with a lower PI tend to be silt, and those with a PI of 0 (non-plastic) tend to have little or no silt or clay.)
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Plasticity Index

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The Point Load Test produces the Point Load Test Index (Is50), which can be correlated with the uniaxial compressive strength (UCS) of rock.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Point Load Test Index

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Ratio of the transverse contraction of a body to its longitudinal extension when stretched. Typical values in minerals are from 0.15 to 0.3 (Carbonates:0.15, Sandstones:0.2, Shales:0.25).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Poisson Ratio

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The value of pore pressure measured in the field after dissipation of induced excess pore pressure. Could also be from CPTu test
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Equilibrium Pore Water Pressure (U0)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The pore-water pressure acting at the center of the membrane before the insertion of the DMT blade (often assumed as hydrostatic below the water table surface).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Estimated Pore Water Pressure

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Measured pore pressure from u1 transducer on tip.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Pore Water Pressure (U1)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Measured pore pressure from u2 transducer behind tip.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Pore Water Pressure (U2)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Measured pore pressure from u3 transducer behind sleeve.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Pore Water Pressure (U3)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Result from a Consolidation Test. This test is performed to determine the magnitude and rate of void ratio change for a laterally confined soil specimen that is subjected to different vertical pressures. From the measured data, the consolidation curve (pressure-void ratio relationship) can be plotted. This specific value is used for a specific portion of the log vertical pressure - void ratio curve to signify the largest value of stress that sample has experienced before the performance of this test. It is a calculation results usually obtained by a construction technique using laboratory test results.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Preconsolidation Pressure

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Value derived from a pressure filtration test
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Pressure Filtration Coefficient

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Flow of water produced by pumping; recorded in pump tests
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Pumping rate

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Result from a Consolidation Test. This test is performed to determine the magnitude and rate of void ratio change for a laterally confined soil specimen that is subjected to different vertical pressures. From the measured data, the consolidation curve (pressure-void ratio relationship) can be plotted. This specific value is used for a specific portion of the log vertical pressure - void ratio curve to signify a response due to the unloading and reloading of a sample that is on the virgin curve.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Recompression Index

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A 'measure of the ability of chemical/biochemical systems to oxidize (lose electrons) or reduce (gain electrons).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Redox Potential

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The density of a granular specimen relative to its maximum and minimum density (or void ratio)
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Density, Relative

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A measure of the resisting power of a specified material to the flow of an electric current.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Electrical Resistivity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The open space in a rock divided by the total rock volume.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Rock Porosity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The Schmidt Hardness Test utilizes a hammer mass launched against an impact plunger. The amount of hammer mass rebound depends on the hardness of the test piece. This rebound amount is then shown on a scale of 10 to 100.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Schmidt Hardness Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: the ratio of the strength of the soil in the undisturbed state to that of the soil in the remolded state.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Sensitivity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Setting time for grout
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Set Time

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The peak shear resistance of an intact specimen when pore fluid pressures, generated during the course of shearing the soil, are able to dissipate during shearing. It also applies where no pore water exists in the soil (the soil is dry) and hence pore fluid pressures are negligible.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Peak Drained Shear Strength

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The peak shear strength of an intact specimen when no volume change is allowed during the tests. The value can be measured in the lab and in the field. In both cases, the value can be calculated from different tests.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Peak Undrained Shear Strength

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A measure of the shear strength of the soil for which the shear stress remains essentially constant with increasing shear displacement andwhen no volume change is allowed during the tests.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Residual Undrained Shear Strength

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The velocity of a shear wave (Vs); a shear wave is a type of seismic wave in which the particle motion is perpendicular to the direction of propagation in a horizontal plane ; also called S-wave or secondary wave.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Shear Velocity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The height of the rebound travel of the Scleroscope hammer is measured on a graduated scale. The scale of the rebound is arbitrarily chosen and consists on Shore units, divided into 100 parts, which represent the average rebound from pure hardened high-carbon steel. The scale is continued higher than 100 to include metals having greater hardness.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Shore Hardness Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The amount specimen shrinkage, reported as a percentage of total volume
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Shrinkage

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The shrinkage limit (SL) is the water content below which a soil undergoes no further volume change.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Shrinkage Limit

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The ratio of a given volume change expressed as a percentage of the dry volume to the corresponding change in water content above the shrinkage limit.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Shrinkage Ratio

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The Slake Durability Index predicts the long-term durability of the rock specimens, to establish weathering and degradation characteristics of each rock type, and to assess the impact of water on the rock degradation.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Slake Durability Index

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Value of stress measured on sleeve of cone during penetration
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Sleeve Friction

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Amount of slump of grout sample
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Slump

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Soil moisture content measured by sensor (eg CPT)
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Soil Moisture Content

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Soil suction value
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Soil Suction

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A value derived from a dilatometer test, using the dilatometer modulus and material index.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Soil Type

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The apparent specific gravity is designated Ga and is the ratio of the weight in air of a unit volume of the impermeable portion of aggregate to the weight in air of an equal volume of distilled water, both at a stated temperature. The impermeable portion of a porous material, such as most large soil grains, includes the solid material plus impermeable pores or voids within the particles.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Apparent Specific Gravity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The bulk specific gravity is designated Gm and is the ratio of the weight in air of a unit volume of aggregate (including permeable and impermeable voids in the particles, but not the voids between the particles) to the weight of an equal volume of distilled water at a stated temperature.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Bulk Specific Gravity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The specific gravity of solids (Gs) is the bulk density of the solid particles relative to the density of water. It is a required parameter to assess void ratio. Its value is a function of the mineralogy of the solid particles. It is commonly assumed by geotechnical engineers.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Specific Gravity of Solids

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Sulfate content of soil or groundwater by laboratory testing (corrosivity series). USE THIS ENTRY WHEN THE SOURCE DOES NOT STATE THE EXTRACTION BASIS - common in practice, and the case for the Jazera project record (GBL-24136), which reports a sulfate content in ppm without saying whether it is water- or acid-soluble. Where the basis IS known, prefer the specific entry instead: sulfate_water_soluble or sulfate_acid_soluble. The distinction is not cosmetic - the two can differ by an order of magnitude on the same material, and BS 8500 / BRE Special Digest 1 derive their ACEC class from a particular one of them.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Sulfate Content

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The contraction of a gel accompanied by the separating out of liquid. It is calculated as a percent of volume or mass loss.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Syneresis

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The syneresis value of a gel specimen divided by its surface area; accounts for variability in syneresis of a gel depending on the amount of the gel exposed to air. Calculated as mass loss divided by surface area
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Surface Area Normalized Syneresis

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Time until pore pressure reaches the halfway pressure (u50) between starting dynamic pore pressure and equilibrium pore pressure
diggs:Definition.gml:name: T50

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Measured temperature
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Temperature

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A measure of the resistance of aggregate crushing.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Ten Percent Fines Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The maximum stress a material can withstand before breaking under tensile (pulling) forces
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Tensile strength

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Thrust force required to advance the dilatometer to the test depth. This force is exclusive of soil or other friction along the push rods. This thrust is referred to as qd.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Thrust

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Time instant of measurement
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Time

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A measure of stress measured at tip of cone during penetration
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Tip Resistance

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Tip resistance corrected for u2 pore pressure measurement
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Corrected Tip Resistance

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Torque: The rotational force applied by the drill rig.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Torque

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Pressure measured with a transducer
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Transducer Pressure

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Pore pressure midway between dynamic pore pressure and equilibrium pore pressure
diggs:Definition.gml:name: U50

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The Unified Soil Classification group name, including any modifiers as defined in Figures 1,2 and 3 of ASTM D2487 or Figures 1 and 2 of ASTM D2488, eg "Silty sand" or "Gravelly silt with sand".
diggs:Definition.gml:name: USCS Group Name

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The two-letter symbol of soil type of the Unified Soil Classification System, used in engineering and geology to describe the texture and grain size of a soil.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: USCS Group Symbol

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The two letter symbol of soil type of the Unified Soil Classification System of material passing 425 micron screen
diggs:Definition.gml:name: USCS Symbol Passing 425 Screen

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Total vertical stress at the center of the membrane before the insertion of the DMT blade, generally calculated from unit weights estimated using the DMT results.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Total Vertical Stress

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The amount of material observed
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Volume

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The amount of volume reduced between observation steps
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Volume Loss

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The decrease in volume of a soil mass when the water content is reduced from a given percentage to the shrinkage limit and which is expressed as percentage of dry volume of the soil mass.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Volumetric Shrinkage

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Descriptive result of a washout test
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Washout Result

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Also referred to as moisture content, this is the mass of water divided by the mass of the solids, expressed as a percentage. Use of this parameter is for natural conditions. Determined in a laboratory or via sensor.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Natural Water Content

diggs:Definition.gml:description: This is a result of a compaction test. It is defined as the moisture content at the maximum dry unit weight as measured when a specific type and amount of energy is used for the compaction test. This is also the value of the compaction moisture content when the soils achieves the maximum dry unit weight.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Optimum Water Content

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Measured depth to water below datum, typically directly observed or computed from a pressure transducer
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Water Depth

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Measured elevation of water level, typically directly observed or computed from a pressure transducer.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Water Elevation

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Amount of carbon (as a percent) in a soil that is easily oxidized as defined in AASHTO Standard T 194.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Easily Oxidized Carbon

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Amount of carbon in a soil (as a percent) as defined in AASHTO Standard T 194.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Total Carbon

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Amount of easily oxidized organic matter (as a percent) in a soil as defined in AASHTO Standard T 194.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Easily Oxidized Organic Matter

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Amount of organic matter (as a percent) in a soil as defined in AASHTO Standard T 194.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Total Organic Matter

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Determined by a one-dimensional swell or collapse test, this is the swell strain corresponding to a vertical stress of 1 kPa (20 lbf/ft2).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Free Swell Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Determined by a one-dimensional swell or collapse test, this is stress corresponding to zero strain.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Swell Pressure

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The rapid method equivalent of percent compaction; the comparison of in-place density to laboratory derived maximum density.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: D Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The comparison of field compactive effort to standard laboratory compactive effort.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: C Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The difference in water content between the field and the optimum water content of a soil.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Water Content Difference

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Grain diameter corresponding to 84 percent passing. Intermediate value used to report other results.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: d84

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Grain diameter corresponding to 90 percent passing. Intermediate value used to report other results.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: d90

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The percentage of particles that pass the 75 mm sieve and are retained on the 19mm sieve (<75 mm and >19mm).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: percent coarse gravel

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The percentage of particles that pass the 19 mm sieve and are retained on the 4.75mm sieve (<19 mm and >4.75mm).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: percent fine gravel

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The percentage of particles thatpass the #4 sieve and are retained on the #10 sieve (<4.75 mm and >2 mm).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: percent coarse sand

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The percentage of particles thatpass the #10 sieve and are retained on the #40 sieve (<2 mm and >0.425 mm).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: percent medium sand

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The percentage of particles thatpass the #40 sieve and are retained on the #200 sieve (<0.425 mm and >0.075 mm).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: percent fine sand

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The percentage of particles that pass the 75mm sieve and are retained on the #10 sieve (<75 mm and >0.075 mm).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: percent gravel aashto

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The percentage of particles that pass the #10 sieve and are retained on the #40 sieve (<2 mm and >0.425 mm).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: percent coarse sand aashto

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The percentage of particles that pass the #40 sieve and are retained on the #200 sieve (<0.425 mm and >0.075 mm).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: percent fine sand aashto

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Downward vertical displacement of a point on the ground surface, within the ground, or on a supported structure, measured against a stated datum and reference time. Positive downward. The single measured quantity behind post-construction settlement monitoring, the measured half of a measured-versus-predicted comparison, and the subject of a settlement acceptance criterion; its predicted counterpart is the typed diggs:PredictedSettlement object, which this does not duplicate.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Settlement

diggs:ValueBinding.diggs:realizedValueXpath: let $r := $evidence/diggs:outcome/*[1], $x := diggs:series($r, 'applied_stress'), $y := diggs:series($r, 'settlement'), $p := diggs:series($r, 'loading_phase') return for $i in 1 to count($y) return if ($p[$i]?2 = 'loading') then [$x[$i]?2, $y[$i]?2] else ()

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The difference in settlement between two points, measured. The separation the difference is taken over is not part of this value: where a criterion expresses the limit as a gradient or angular distortion, the criterion's own basis and baseLength carry it, exactly as they do for the predicted form on diggs:DesignRITreatedAreaType.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Differential settlement

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Measured settlement of the treated ground divided by the settlement of the equivalent untreated ground. The measured counterpart of diggs:DesignRITreatedAreaType/settlementEfficacy; which definition of the ratio is in use is stated by that design element's settlementEfficacyDefinition, since a measured value is only comparable against the prediction under the same definition.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Settlement reduction ratio (measured)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Pore water pressure measured by an installed piezometer over time. Deliberately distinct from the pore_pressure_u1/_u2/_u3 and pore_pressure_est/_equil entries in this dictionary, all of which are cone-penetration dissipation-stage labels tied to a transducer position on a CPT tip and meaningless for a standalone instrument.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Pore water pressure (monitored)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The fraction of total applied load carried by the reinforcement rather than by the surrounding soil. Dimensionless, 0 to 1. Named by a diggs:PerformanceCriterion stating a minimum, which is how a design requirement on load sharing is expressed.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Reinforcement load fraction

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The load at which the rate of settlement under sustained load becomes unacceptably large - conventionally the load level above which the rate of creep settlement increases sharply with each load increment, taken from a static load test loading schedule that includes sustained-load (creep) readings at one or more increments. A result of diggs:StaticLoadTest.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Critical Creep Load

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The ratio of applied bearing pressure to plate settlement (k) derived from a plate-bearing load test - ASTM D1195/D1196's characteristic output. Force per unit volume (pressure/deflection), reported in units such as kN/m3 or pci.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Modulus of Subgrade Reaction

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The deformation modulus derived from the load-settlement curve of the FIRST loading cycle of a two-cycle plate-bearing load test, per DIN 18134. Reflects the initial condition of the ground or platform material, including particle rearrangement and closure of air voids.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Deformation Modulus, First Load (Ev1)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The deformation modulus derived from the load-settlement curve of the SECOND loading cycle of a two-cycle plate-bearing load test, per DIN 18134. Primarily reflects the repeatable elastic behaviour of the ground or platform material after the first cycle's initial compression. The ratio Ev2/Ev1 (see #deformation_modulus_first_load) is DIN 18134's own reported indicator of the degree of compaction achieved.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Deformation Modulus, Second Load (Ev2)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The depth from the pile/element head to an interpreted discontinuity, void, necking, or other change in cross-section identified from a low-strain integrity test record. Absent where the test found no defect and the reflection at the recorded travel time is interpreted as the pile toe instead. A result of diggs:LowStrainIntegrityTest.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Defect Depth

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The as-built effective radius (or equivalent cross-sectional dimension) at a given depth, interpreted from a thermal integrity profiling temperature record by comparing the measured heat signature against the response expected for the design cross-section - a reduction indicates necking or a concrete deficiency, an increase indicates bulging. A result of diggs:ThermalIntegrityProfiling.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Effective Radius

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Horizontal displacement of the load application point (or another stated gauge point) on a deep foundation element under a static lateral load test, measured against a stated datum. Distinct from properties.xml#settlement, which is explicitly vertical. A result of diggs:LateralLoadTest.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Lateral Deflection

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Magnesium content by lab testing (corrosivity series). Completes the chemistry set the ground-aggressivity classifications are derived from: EN 206 grades chemical attack partly on magnesium ion content, and BS 8500 derives its ACEC class from sulfate AND magnesium together via BRE Special Digest 1, so an exposureClassification could be stated without the measurement that justifies it. Added at R10 from the Jazera project record (GBL-24136), which reports 571-954 ppm alongside its sulfate, chloride and pH results. USE THIS ENTRY WHEN THE SOURCE DOES NOT STATE THE EXTRACTION BASIS, as that record does not; where it is known to be the water-soluble determination of BS 1377-3 Clause 10, prefer magnesium_water_soluble instead.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Magnesium Content

diggs:Definition.gml:description: California Bearing Ratio (CBR), expressed as a percentage, of the measured pressure required to achieve a given penetration into a soil specimen divided by the pressure required to achieve the same penetration on a standard crushed rock material. This generic term carries no built-in compaction, density, or soaking condition - use it together with a qualifier property (eg. percent of maximum dry density, soaking condition) to state the specific condition this value was determined under. Where a common condition applies, prefer the corresponding named term instead (eg. #cbr_at_95_pct_mdd).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: California Bearing Ratio

diggs:Definition.gml:description: California Bearing Ratio (CBR), expressed as a percentage, interpolated at 95% of the maximum dry density (MDD) established by an associated compaction test (eg. ASTM D1557, Modified Proctor), from a series of specimens compacted at different efforts and, where soaking is specified by the test method, soaked prior to penetration testing.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: CBR at 95% Maximum Dry Density

diggs:Definition.gml:description: California Bearing Ratio (CBR), expressed as a percentage, interpolated at 90% of the maximum dry density (MDD) established by an associated compaction test (eg. ASTM D1557, Modified Proctor), from a series of specimens compacted at different efforts and, where soaking is specified by the test method, soaked prior to penetration testing.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: CBR at 90% Maximum Dry Density

diggs:Definition.gml:description: California Bearing Ratio (CBR), expressed as a percentage, interpolated over the 98-100% band of the maximum dry density (MDD) established by an associated compaction test (eg. ASTM D1557, Modified Proctor), from a series of specimens compacted at different efforts and, where soaking is specified by the test method, soaked prior to penetration testing.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: CBR at 98-100% Maximum Dry Density

diggs:Definition.gml:description: California Bearing Ratio (CBR), expressed as a percentage, of a specimen tested at its as-compacted (100% of maximum dry density) density and moisture content without soaking, representing as-built or short-term strength rather than the soaked design condition standard test methods normally specify.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: CBR As Compacted (Unsoaked)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The minimum apparent resistivity value among the readings taken during an in-situ electrical resistivity test at a station, used together with the maximum apparent resistivity to characterize the resistivity range for a corrosivity classification (eg. Palmer, 1974).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Minimum Apparent Resistivity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The maximum apparent resistivity value among the readings taken during an in-situ electrical resistivity test at a station, used together with the minimum apparent resistivity to characterize the resistivity range for a corrosivity classification (eg. Palmer, 1974).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Maximum Apparent Resistivity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A qualitative soil corrosivity rating for buried metal, assigned from the apparent resistivity range measured by an in-situ electrical resistivity test according to the correlation published by Palmer (1974): 0-10 ohm.m Very Severe, 11-20 Severe, 21-50 Moderate, 51-100 Mild, 101+ Very Mild.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Corrosivity Classification (Palmer, 1974)
diggs:Definition.diggs:reference: Palmer, J.D. (1974). Soil Resistivity - Measurement and Analysis. Material Performance, Vol. 13.

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A material's ability to conduct heat, determined for soil or soft rock by the thermal needle probe method (ASTM D5334, IEEE Std 442).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Thermal Conductivity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The reciprocal of thermal conductivity - a material's opposition to heat flow per unit length - determined for soil or soft rock by the thermal needle probe method (ASTM D5334, IEEE Std 442).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Thermal Resistivity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Water-soluble sulfate content of soil or groundwater - the fraction released by a water extract, conventionally the 2:1 water:soil extract of BS 1377-3 Clause 7, and the quantity determined by ASTM C1580 and AASHTO T 290. Use in preference to the generic sulfate_content whenever the source states that the determination was water-soluble. Distinguish from sulfate_acid_soluble: the two can differ by an order of magnitude on the same material, and BS 8500 / BRE Special Digest 1 ACEC classification depends on which was measured.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Sulfate Content, Water-Soluble

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Acid-soluble sulfate content of soil - the fraction released by acid digestion, per BS 1377-3 Clause 7, and generally the larger of the two determinations because it mobilises sparingly-soluble sulfate minerals such as gypsum that a water extract leaves behind. Use in preference to the generic sulfate_content whenever the source states that the determination was acid-soluble. Distinct again from total sulfur and from the sulfide determinations of the same clause, which are different analytes rather than different extractions.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Sulfate Content, Acid-Soluble

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Water-soluble chloride content of soil or groundwater - the fraction released by a water extract, per BS 1377-3 Clause 9 and AASHTO T 291. Use in preference to the generic chloride_content whenever the source states that the determination was water-soluble.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Chloride Content, Water-Soluble

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Acid-soluble chloride content of soil - the fraction released by acid digestion, per BS 1377-3 Clause 9. Use in preference to the generic chloride_content whenever the source states that the determination was acid-soluble.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Chloride Content, Acid-Soluble

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Water-soluble magnesium content of soil or groundwater, per BS 1377-3 Clause 10 - which specifies the water-soluble determination only, so for magnesium this is the basis a BS 1377-3 result will normally be on even when the report does not say so. Use in preference to the generic magnesium_content whenever the source confirms it. Magnesium matters because BS 8500 derives its ACEC class from sulfate and magnesium together via BRE Special Digest 1, and EN 206 grades chemical attack partly on magnesium ion content.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Magnesium Content, Water-Soluble

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Total organic carbon (TOC) content of soil, per BS 1377-3 Clause 5 - the carbon held in organic compounds, determined after removing carbonate carbon. Distinct from total_carbon and easily_oxidized_carbon, which are the AASHTO T 194 wet-combustion determinations bound to OrganicMatterByWetCombustionTest, and distinct again from LOI (loss on ignition, Clause 6) and total_organic_matter, which measure organic MATTER rather than the carbon within it.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Total Organic Carbon

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Carbonate content of soil, per BS 1377-3 Clause 8, usually expressed as equivalent calcium carbonate. Relevant both to ground aggressivity - carbonate buffers acidity and moderates the pH a corrosion assessment reads - and to the identification of calcareous and cemented soils. The Jazera site's sabkha and calcareous sands are exactly the materials for which this is normally reported, though this determination is not in the project record.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Carbonate Content

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Total sulfur content of soil, per BS 1377-3 Clause 7 - all sulfur present, in every oxidation state, not only that recoverable as sulfate. The upper bound on sulfate that could develop if reduced sulfur compounds oxidise, which is why it is reported for pyritic and sabkha ground. A DIFFERENT ANALYTE from sulfate_content and its water- and acid-soluble variants, not another extraction of the same one.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Total Sulfur

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Total sulfide content of soil, also called total reduced sulfur, per BS 1377-3 Clause 7 - sulfur held in reduced form, which on exposure to air can oxidise to sulfate and acidify the ground. Reported where pyrite or organic-rich anaerobic deposits are suspected. Distinct from sulfide_acid_soluble, which recovers only the monosulfide fraction.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Total Sulfide

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Acid-soluble sulfide content of soil - the monosulfide fraction released by acid digestion, per BS 1377-3 Clause 7. A subset of total_sulfide: it does not recover disulfides such as pyrite, so the two differ substantially in pyritic ground and should not be used interchangeably.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Sulfide Content, Acid-Soluble

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Total dissolved solids (TDS) of groundwater, per BS 1377-3 Clause 11 - the mass of dissolved material remaining after evaporation of a filtered sample. A summary measure of groundwater salinity, read alongside the individual ion determinations (sulfate, chloride, magnesium) rather than in place of them.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Total Dissolved Solids

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Total weight (of solids and water) divided by total volume of material, representing natural conditions. Parallels bulk_density, but reported strictly as a force per volume (unit weight) rather than interchangeably as mass per volume.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Unit Weight, Bulk (Natural)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Weight of solids divided by total volume. Parallels dry_density, but reported strictly as a force per volume (unit weight) rather than interchangeably as mass per volume.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Unit Weight, Dry

diggs:Definition.gml:description: This is a result of a compaction test. It is defined as the maximum dry unit weight that is measured when a specific type and amount of energy is used for the compaction test. This is also the value of the compacted dry unit weight when the soil is at the optimum moisture content. Parallels dry_density_max, but reported strictly as a force per volume (unit weight) rather than interchangeably as mass per volume.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Maximum Unit Weight

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The maximum compressive force carried by a specimen during an unconfined compressive strength test - the force from which the compressive strength is calculated, as that force divided by the cross-sectional area of the specimen.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Maximum axial load

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The secant modulus of a specimen at half its unconfined compressive strength: E50 is half the unconfined compressive strength divided by the axial strain at which the compressive stress reaches that half value. Where the start of the stress-strain curve has an inflection from specimen seating, the strain origin is corrected before E50 is taken.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Deformation modulus E50

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The factor by which the measured compressive strength of a cylindrical specimen is multiplied where its length-to-diameter ratio is 1.75 or less, interpolated between tabulated ratios. The 2009 edition of ASTM C39 gives 0.98 at a ratio of 1.75, 0.96 at 1.50, 0.93 at 1.25 and 0.87 at 1.00.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Length-to-diameter correction factor

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Reading of a displacement gage (dial gage or displacement transducer) at one gage point, expressed as a displacement. Where several gages are read together, each is a separate property distinguished by its propertyName (for example "Dial Gage 1"); their average is reported the same way.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Gage Reading

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Normal stress applied to the ground or element through the bearing area of a load test (a plate or loaded footprint) at the time of the reading.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Applied Stress

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Hydraulic pressure read at the gauge of the jack applying a test load. Converted to load or stress through the jack calibration.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Jack Pressure

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Whether a load test reading or increment belongs to seating, loading, unloading or reloading.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Loading Phase

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Mass of an item of test equipment as weighed, for example a bearing plate or a jack resting on the tested element.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Equipment Mass

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Value of the reference standard applied to the item at one calibration point, in the unit of the quantity calibrated (for example bar for a pressure gauge).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Calibration Reference Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Value the item under calibration indicated at one calibration point, in the unit of the quantity calibrated.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Calibration Indicated Value

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Difference between the value the item indicated and the reference value applied, at one calibration point, as reported on the certificate.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Calibration Deviation

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Expanded uncertainty of the calibration at one point, at the coverage factor stated for the calibration (coverage_factor).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Calibration Expanded Uncertainty

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Smallest change in the quantity measured that the instrument displays, as stated on the calibration certificate.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Instrument Resolution

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Largest expanded uncertainty over the calibrated range, as stated on the calibration certificate, in the unit of the quantity calibrated.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Maximum Expanded Uncertainty

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Factor multiplying the standard uncertainty to give the expanded uncertainty reported; k = 2 corresponds to a coverage probability of approximately 95 %.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Coverage Factor

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Lower limit of the range over which the instrument was calibrated, in the unit of the quantity calibrated.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Calibrated Range Minimum

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Upper limit of the range over which the instrument was calibrated, in the unit of the quantity calibrated.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Calibrated Range Maximum

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The tolerance the instrument is accepted to, as stated on the calibration certificate - a limit or a reference to the manufacturer's specification.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Acceptance Tolerance

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Area of the hydraulic jack ram, as stated on the calibration certificate, used to convert jack pressure to force.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Jack Ram Area

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Air temperature in the laboratory or on site while a calibration was performed. State the permitted variation as the minimum and maximum value.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Ambient Temperature

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Relative humidity of the air while a calibration was performed. State the permitted variation as the minimum and maximum value.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Relative Humidity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The depth from the pile or element head to the toe reflection of a low-strain integrity test record: the deepest reflection of the record, found by working up from the bottom of the record, taken at its first amplitude maximum (or at its starting deflection where the start pulse of the record is referenced to its starting deflection). Reading from the bottom separates the toe from internal defects, which lie above it. The depth is calculated from the travel time and the assumed wave speed. A result of diggs:LowStrainIntegrityTest. Compare with the length of the element through toe_depth_deviation; defect_depth is the depth of a reflection above the toe.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Toe Depth

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The difference between the toe depth of a low-strain integrity test and the as-built length of the element, without sign, as a percentage of the as-built length. The assumed wave speed alone can move a reflected depth by about ten percent, which sets the order of a limit on this property.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Toe Depth Deviation

diggs:ValueBinding.diggs:realizedValueXpath: let $t := diggs:otherMeasurementProperty/diggs:AuthorizedParameter[diggs:parameterName/@codeSpace[ends-with(., '#toe_depth')]]/diggs:parameterValue, $l := diggs:procedure/*/diggs:referenceLength return if (exists($t) and exists($l)) then abs(number($t) - number($l)) * 100 div number($l) else ()

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The height of a reflection in a low-strain integrity test record relative to the height of the initial impact peak, both read from the same record. A reflection of the same sign as the impact, above the toe, indicates a reduction in impedance - a neck, a crack or poor concrete - and its relative height approximates the reflection coefficient where the amplification of the record balances the toe reflection against the impact. Stated for the largest such reflection above the toe.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Relative Reflection Amplitude

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The velocity of the head of a pile or element in a low-strain integrity test record as evaluated: averaged over the impacts, amplified as the procedure states and normalized so that the impact peak has a fixed height. A number without a unit, comparable only with the impact of the same record. A column of the depth-indexed result of diggs:LowStrainIntegrityTest.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Normalized Velocity

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The force applied to the head of a pile or element in a low-strain integrity test with an instrumented hammer, normalized to the same scale as the normalized velocity of the record. A number without a unit. A column of the result of diggs:LowStrainIntegrityTest.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Normalized Force

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The force applied to the head of a pile or element by the hammer of a low-strain integrity test, measured by an instrumented hammer. A column of the result of diggs:LowStrainIntegrityTest.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Impact Force

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The impedance of a pile or element at a depth relative to its impedance at the head, as reconstructed from a low-strain integrity test record; 1 where the section and the concrete equal those at the head. A column of the depth-indexed result of diggs:LowStrainIntegrityTest.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Relative Impedance

diggs:Definition.gml:description: A frequency at which a frequency-domain record is stated - for example a row of the mobility record of a transient response low-strain integrity test (diggs:LowStrainIntegrityTest/frequencyResponse).
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Frequency

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The ratio of the velocity transform to the force transform at the head of a pile or element at a frequency, in a transient response low-strain integrity test: velocity per force (s/kg, equal to m/(N.s)). A column of diggs:LowStrainIntegrityTest/frequencyResponse. Not the fluid mobility of a porous medium.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Mobility

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The mean mobility over the range of resonant frequencies of a transient response low-strain integrity test record. For a uniform element it approximates the reciprocal of the product of concrete density, wave speed and cross-sectional area, so it reflects the section and the quality of the concrete.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Characteristic Mobility

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The ratio of force to displacement at the head of a pile or element at low frequency, read from the initial slope of the mobility record of a transient response low-strain integrity test. It reflects the element and the soil around it.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Dynamic Stiffness

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The ratio of the peak mobility to the characteristic mobility of a transient response low-strain integrity test record. A number without a unit.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Mobility Ratio

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The height of the toe reflection of a low-strain integrity test record relative to the height of the initial impact peak, both read from the same record: 1 where the amplification balances the toe reflection against the impact, above 1 where the record is amplified past that balance and below 1 where it is not amplified up to it. A result of diggs:LowStrainIntegrityTest. See relative_reflection_amplitude.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Relative Toe Amplitude
